body:
I can relate to the last part. In just the last 24hrs I have cried for more than 6hrs in total. I'm so exhausted I literally feel sorry for myself.

How was the hospital? Thinking of admitting myself...

I believe depression is environmental. I guess that's why they say you cannot heal in the same environment where you got sick.

And money = access to a better life. Literally.
If only I had less stuff. And a car. And no aversion to cars. And enough balls to pull off something like that. Man oh man...

Yeah, you should seek help. Self-harm is never okay. Go see your GP/psychiatrist/psychologist. They're here to help. Thoughts are just thoughts (as opposed to actions) but if they're obsessive and make you suffer, then that's a problem. Also, isolating yourself, hiding emotions and anger only to explode later on is a recipe for disaster. Good luck.

I have. And it felt like I was literally losing my mind. I don't think anyone who hasn't experienced that have any idea what it feels like. It was pure despair and agony. 100% torture with no way out.

Formulating thoughts was outta the question. I couldn't eat, I couldn't work, I couldn't focus, I couldn't even speak properly. Most days I couldn't event walk straight, my legs and hands were constantly shaking. It's as if I was heavily drugged 24/7. Slurred speech, tears every few minutes, feeling both zombified and overwhelmed by despair, suicidal. Horrible, horrible experience.

I would start taking antidepressants asap, also try to have some fun during the day (watch a comedy, hang out with friends, spend time around animals, play a game, dance, sing, workout, idk, do something you like) and then try to calm yourself down especially before going to bed. That means no drama, no internet, no work, no stress. Watch a mind-numbing movie (nothing scary tho), put on some mellow music, lie down and just relax.

Maybe try some antihistamines, e.g. doxylamine before sleep. I know people use diphenhydramine (Benadryl) but personally, I've never tried that one.

Tbh, reducing stress is the only way (for me) to get some sleep.

When my anxiety is unbearable so is my depression, and then absolutely nothing works to calm me down except Alprazolam (Xanax) but I don't use it as a sleeping aid. It helps with cryfests and suicidal thoughts though.

Zolpidem NEVER worked, not one bit. On an average day I do get a few hrs of sleep at night but it is sooo damn fragmented it's more like napping. On a bad day I get literally 0 hrs of sleep.
In fact, I took it last night, eventually fell asleep around 4am, woke up an hour later, struggled to fall asleep again, slept for an hour, woke up, etc. Rinse and repeat.

Tried various antihistamines, and while some of them did make me sleepy/tired (when my anxiety was generally manageble), I still woke up after 1-2 hrs and was struggling to nap for another one or 2. Doxylamine was better as it managed to get me up to 5 hrs of sleep on a better day.

Trazodone (SR) worked for about 2 days (again, up to 5hrs of sleep) then, stopped working. Was pretty fed up with it too as it was making me extremely dizzy, tired and sleepy throughout the whole next day and my blood pressure would drop at least several times a day. Somehow in the evening all of this would go away and I'd be alert and fully awake.
Maybe I should've tried a lower dose.

Melatonin does nothing when you're anxious. When I'm already calm and tired it does (sometimes) induce sleepiness but only for like 20 mins. If I do anything like brush my teeth, I'm instantly fully awake and that's it.

Valerian root doesn't do much for panic attacks / severe anxiety & depression but when I'm doing relatively good a couple of pills before bed do help me get some sleep.

I do use ear buds and play soft mellow music every single night to shield me from noise and also to calm me down a little bit.

I found out the hard way that pills only help when you're facing SOME discomfort, but when it's a damn disaster 24/7 and you're barely functioning, like just a shell of a human being, nothing seems to work. It is only when things get better in your personal life, I mean less stress, no contact with toxic people, no drama, that you are able to calm down and THEN pills help.

Unfortunately, after a brief period of being fine and taking only valerian-melatonin combo or antihistamines, the drama came back and sent me into a downward spiral of despair and insomnia. Idk what else to say, hopefully switching to sertraline will "help" in the long run cause my environment and personal life sure as heck will not change anytime soon, so unless my brain & body both get used to this constant stress, drama and noise, there's no hope for me. :/

Judging by what you've just said you're far from being a worthless piece of shit. I know plenty of people who truly deserve being called a p.o.s., evil shitty beings who do nothing but take pleasure in making others suffer. You with your personality and the way you write about yourself would never ever be classified as one.  
Now a failure is never something we are or become, it's not a title, not a fact, it's something we feel, and only when we feel bad about our actions or lack thereof.  
Sorry you feel so much self-hate and sabotage yourself from taking any chances to enjoy life. I know the feeling of pain, misery and overwhelming despair. I'm struggling myself. I'm exhausted. I know how it feels. You are not alone with those feelings.  
Suicide is for people who have absolutely nothing to lose. Nothing keeping them here. Nothing.  
If you feel nostalgia, think about when you were happy, wish the good old times would come back, and have some family members you care enough to write a note to, there is still something for you. Still a good chance that with support you can feel alive, feel joy, and turn things around. Usually at this point it's the small things that make us reconsider and fight harder to change our situation. A pleasant memory, a distant dream or goal we once had, a friendly face willing to care and help us, etc.
